newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB recommends move grain to diked area, high bins.
newsitem.headline: CWB recommends move grain to diked area, high bins.

text.p: Farmers in the Red River Valley were encouraged to move their grain to diked areas and bins on high ground ahead of what may be a serious flood this spring, a Canadian Wheat Board official said.

"We're encouraging them to move their grain to higher ground. There's a lot of grain bins out in the field where it's low ground, so in some of the yards they've got higher ground or they're diked," CWB area representative for the Eastern Manitoba Region Bert Dupasquier told Reuters.
Snowfall in the Red River watershed is twice to three times more than normal, Manitoba Water Resources Branch said.
The CWB, Manitoba Pool Elevators and provincial government officials briefed farmers in Domain, Man., Tuesday morning, Dupasquier said.
One hundred percent of the CWB's first three quarterly delivery contracts for grain in Eastern Manitoba was moved out of the flood zone ahead of last year's thaw, he said.
Pacific port backlogs and congestion in the Prairies along with a record grain and oilseed harvest means some grain will likely remain in the flood zone this spring, he added.
"We don't have the car supply now and last year's crop was smaller," Dupasquier said.
Delivery calls for Series A grain contracts were increased to 80 percent from 60 percent, Dupasquier said.
Sixty percent of Series B grain deliveries will be accepted at area elevators, he added.
